extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners; PR/communications professionals who write or evaluate news releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing news releases, media alerts, and pitch materials that meet newsroom and industry expectations; emphasizes format, content, distribution, and ethical/legal norms to maximize pickup. Focused on practical, journalist-friendly release construction and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterhead identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuer's logo, address, and contact info on the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify the releasing organization on the first page so journalists immediately know the source; use official letterhead or equivalent branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing line
rubrics_metrics.description: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE" or specific embargo date/time at top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a timing indicator at the top to make embargo status and release timing explicit; use exact embargo date/time when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact block
rubrics_metrics.description: Name, phone, email, time-zone, after-hours availability of media-relations officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full media-contact details including time-zone and after-hours availability so journalists can reach sources quickly; include alternate contacts if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject-verb-object; concrete; under 12 words; no all-caps; no marketing adjectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a concise, journalistic headline (S-V-O) that is concrete and newsy. Avoid all-caps styling and promotional superlatives that read like advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subhead (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: One-line elaboration that adds dimension the headline lacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single-line subhead to add an important detail or secondary angle not captured in the headline; keep it tight and complementary, not repetitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: "CITY, State (or country) — Day Month Year —" before the lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a dateline (city, state/country and full date) placed before the lead sentence to follow journalistic convention and signal locale and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Single sentence; under 35 words; answers who/what/when/where/why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a tight one-sentence lead that quickly supplies the essential facts (who, what, when, where, why). Aim for under 35 words for readability and to facilitate journalists' scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted-pyramid body
rubrics_metrics.description: Most important first; next-most second; supporting fourth-fifth; boilerplate at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize body copy in inverted-pyramid order so the crucial information appears early; supporting details and background follow, with the standardized boilerplate closing the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote rule
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one direct quote, preferably from a senior named source with title; second quote from independent source where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one attributable direct quote to give the release a human voice and provide usable copy for journalists. Prefer quotes from senior, named sources and add an independent-source quote when feasible to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized "About [issuer]" paragraph at the end, ≤100 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with a concise organizational boilerplate (about paragraph) of no more than about 100 words containing essential background and contact pointers; keep it consistent across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: End mark
rubrics_metrics.description: "###" or "—END—" or "—30—" centered after final paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conventional end mark centered after the final paragraph to signal the end of the release for newsroom intake systems and editors. Common markers include ###, —END—, or —30—.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-value alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each release should be evaluable against classical news values (timeliness, prominence, proximity, conflict, human interest, novelty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write and evaluate releases by asking which traditional news values they meet; emphasize the strongest applicable values to make the release newsworthy to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-angle option
rubrics_metrics.description: For nationally-distributed releases, supply a local-angle version when distributing to community papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt national news to local contexts by supplying localized versions (local angles, quotes, or datelines) for community outlets to increase relevance and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single key idea
rubrics_metrics.description: One central message; secondary points support, not compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the release on a single primary message; ensure secondary information supports rather than dilutes the main point to avoid confusing journalists or audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice and short sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Average sentence length under 25 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active-voice construction and keep sentences short (average <25 words) for clarity and to match journalistic style; this increases readability and copy-ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Should be readable as journalism, not advertising; no superlatives unless verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write releases that read like news copy rather than promotional copy; avoid unverifiable superlatives and marketing puffery that reduce credibility with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive opening sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids generic openings ("Today, [issuer] announced...") in favor of substantive lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a substantive, distinctive lead sentence rather than formulaic boilerplate to catch editors' attention and immediately convey news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Wilcox-Cameron recommend targeted lists over blast distribution; pickup correlates with relevance to the receiving journalist's beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize well-segmented, beat-focused media lists and targeted outreach instead of mass blasts. Relevance to recipient increases likelihood of pickup and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-format availability
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF for archival, plain-text for wire intake, HTML for online distribution, social-media snippet variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the release in multiple formats suited to different channels: plain text for wire services, PDF for download/archival, HTML for web posting, and short snippets for social distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo (with caption), B-roll where applicable, infographic, fact-sheet attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a multimedia package when relevant—images with captions, video/B-roll, infographics, fact sheets—to increase newsworthiness and make coverage easier for newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Follows PRSA principles (truth, accuracy, disclosure of source, no deception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure releases adhere to professional ethical standards such as those in the PRSA Code of Ethics: be truthful, accurate, disclose sources, and avoid deceptive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism check
rubrics_metrics.description: Original wording, no uncredited reuse from other organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that release copy is original and does not reproduce others' material without attribution; uncredited reuse undermines credibility and ethical standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark / copyright clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: All third-party material properly licensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain licenses or permissions for any third-party copyrighted materials or trademarks included in the release or multimedia attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed releases follow industry norms (Ingelfinger rule, Nature/Science embargo policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing embargoed information, respect established embargo conventions and clearly communicate embargo terms to recipients; understand specific policies of outlets (e.g., academic journal embargo norms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Format compliance and targeted/multiform distribution materially affect newsroom processing and pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases that violate canonical format elements (e.g., missing dateline, no contact block, no end mark) are demoted in routine processing; compliance with format plus clear news value and appropriate distribution increases baseline pickup. The textbook emphasizes that pickup-worthiness is both textual and logistical—targeting and format availability are 'load-bearing.'
